questions.question: The recorder is registered on PreToolUse and PostToolUse only. If someone later registers it on another event (e.g. PostToolUseFailure), what should it do with that payload?

options.label: Keep under raw name (Recommended)
options.description: Append a line with event=<hook_event_name> and the whole payload. Nothing is lost; readers skip unknown kinds, as the amended RFC requires. Current implementation.

options.label: Drop it
options.description: Write nothing for unregistered events. The log only ever holds asked/answered; a future registration silently records nothing until the recorder is extended.

questions.question: Finding 3: `/pr` asks its own questions (trace gate, stop conditions) after Step 1's tail commit, so their decision-log lines stay uncommitted, though RFC D2 says /pr covers them. Which fix?

options.label: Move tail to before Step 6 (Recommended)
options.description: The tail commit runs after the last step that can ask (gates, trace gate), then pushes. D2's claim becomes true. Step 1 keeps its clean check, so a staged leftover still fails there. Pathspec-pinned commit per finding 2.

options.label: Narrow D2's claim
options.description: Keep the tail commit in Step 1; D2 says /pr's own questions reach the next commit, as dialogs after /pr already do. Smaller edit, but those dialogs miss the PR's own committed log.

questions.question: Finding 4: RFC Impact lists `sdd/AUTHORING.md` directory defaults as a ripple for `sdd/decisions/`, and this PR leaves AUTHORING untouched. Which fix?

options.label: Narrow the RFC claim (Recommended)
options.description: AUTHORING's directory table classifies .md files for the docs pipeline; .jsonl never enters it (docs-build and docs-check pass with the log present). Replace the Impact item with that derivation. No AUTHORING edit.

options.label: Add an AUTHORING row
options.description: Add `sdd/decisions/*.jsonl` to Directory defaults as not documentation. Makes the directory discoverable to a reader of AUTHORING, at the cost of a row about a non-.md file in a .md classification table.

options.label: Track as pending on BK-397
options.description: Leave both files as they are; add the AUTHORING ripple to BK-397's pending list for step 2 or 3 to decide.

questions.question: Finding 9: D4.3 promises the PR body renders decisions only from the committed log, but /pr now drafts the body (Step 5) before the tail commit (Step 6). How should it be fixed?

options.label: Move tail before drafting (Recommended)
options.description: Tail commit becomes Step 4, right after the trace gate (Step 3), the last step that can ask. Gather and draft follow it, so a future renderer reads a committed log with no re-render. D4.3 says 'after the tail commit'.

options.label: Keep order, render after
options.description: Tail stays Step 6; D4.3 says step 3 must render after it and update the body. Two writes of the PR body per /pr run, and the renderer has to know about the update.

questions.question: Finding 10, measured: one session spanning two branches blocks branch switches (cases 1 and 2) and gives an add/add merge conflict (case 3). D2 claims logs 'cannot conflict on merge'. What does this PR do?

options.label: Bound claim + track (Recommended)
options.description: D2 states the three measured cases as a bound (one log per session is conflict-free only while the session stays on one branch) and BK-397's pending list gains the storage-design question. No code change here; the remedy is designed with step 2.

options.label: Per-branch file name now
options.description: Name logs <session_id>--<branch>.jsonl. Fixes cases 2 and 3 in this PR; case 1 remains (a dialog after a branch's last commit still blocks switching). Changes D2/D4.0 and the recorder now, another review round.

options.label: Bound claim only
options.description: D2 states the bound; nothing tracked. Cheapest, but the known failure has no owner.

questions.question: Finding 11 (measured): the freshness check's own rebase question dirties the tracked decision log, and `git rebase` then refuses ('cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes'). Fix in the shared Branch freshness check (used by /pr and /fix-pr)?

options.label: Commit tail, then rebase (Recommended)
options.description: Before `git rebase`, commit the log tail with the same pathspec commands /pr Step 4 uses. Measured to rebase cleanly. Adds a small 'decision log' commit when the branch is behind; RFC D2's bound gains the case as handled.

options.label: git rebase --autostash
options.description: One flag, no extra commit. But the stash stack is shared with other sessions and worktrees here, and an autostash that fails to reapply is parked in that shared list.
